assessment: PARTIAL: targeted source review and isolated privacy tests completed; production controls need actual hosting acceptance.
scope: Authentication/session signing, expiry, logout epoch and login throttling
CSRF/origin checks and production Host/HTTPS/proxy trust
Mandatory review/approval/publication transitions and stale-version handling
HTML escaping, content limits, parameterized SQL, static path allowlist
Ollama loopback endpoint, model selection and request transport
SMTP TLS/consent/delivery configuration; actual sending not activated
Current candidates and locally reachable Git history known-signature/private-path scan
Static Docker/Caddy secret, privilege, persistence and network review

issues.title: Cloud model tags were accepted by the local-only drafting client
issues.baseline_proof: A mocked transport recorded model gemma4:cloud in an actual generated request. No cloud inference or external model request occurred. Ollama primary documentation confirms signed-in localhost can route a cloud tag remotely.
issues.fix: Reject model names containing the cloud token before any transport operation. Installed gemma4:e4b requests retain source provenance.

issues.title: Default HTTP transport could route local inference through proxies or redirects
issues.baseline_proof: A synthetic loopback HTTP 302 was followed to a second listener and its JSON was accepted. In a separate reproduction using the original urllib transport with explicit proxy settings and proxy bypass disabled, a loopback proxy received the fictional prompt and absolute Ollama target URL. Neither reproduction used an external destination.
issues.fix: Build the local inference opener with ProxyHandler({}) and an HTTPRedirectHandler that rejects redirects.

review_findings: No additional confirmed authentication, CSRF, SQL injection, HTML escaping or editor state-machine defect found within this targeted review. This is not a full penetration test.
limits: RSS resolves destinations during validation and again during connection; DNS rebinding is a documented residual requiring trusted configured feeds and host egress policy. No DNS-pinning redesign or live rebinding attack was performed.

The local Ollama daemon remains a trusted component. Standard cloud tags are rejected; independently renamed models or a malicious daemon cannot be proven local by tag screening. Disable cloud features in the daemon and use host egress policy for a stronger boundary.
No real public HTTPS, editor CIDR enforcement, server filesystem permissions, container image/OS scanning, off-host encryption, or production recovery was established by this source review.
Known-pattern secret scanning cannot prove no secret ever existed; unreachable objects, remote-only history, entropy analysis and exact private-value comparison are outside this scan.
SMTP testing was mocked elsewhere; no real email was sent by this review.
No original database or private configuration was opened or modified by this review. Only isolated synthetic inputs and ignored temporary proof files were used.
